land.text: Western Australia, which 'on 1 January 1901, following a proclamation by Queen Victoria' joined the Commonwealth

successors.note: The State of Western Australia is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier from 1 January 1901.

capitals.name: Perth
capitals.note: The Swan River Colony page: 'it became the capital city of Western Australia'; the History of Western Australia page: the colony's first settlement 'ultimately became the present-day capital, Perth'. Fremantle (landing 1829) was the port.

correction.text: 'all that part of New Holland which is not included within the territory of New South Wales', that is the land west of the 129th meridian east

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: modern Western Australia, about 3.1 M km2 by the gazetteer's cell count (no infobox area on any page opened). The 129 E western line of New South Wales was set on 16 July 1825 (Territorial evolution of Australia), so the colony's eastern line is that meridian; the pages opened do not date any later change. Settlement was the Swan River district for decades; the colony's border claim covers the whole west.

region.text: all that part of New Holland which is not included within the territory of New South Wales

ledger.note: 1829: the Swan River Colony is established, claiming all of Australia west of New South Wales. 'Captain Charles Fremantle claimed all that part of New Holland which is not included within the territory of New South Wales' for Britain (2 May 1829); a party from Parmelia encamped on Rous Head on 17 June, 'thus establishing the Swan River Colony' (infobox 'Established: 17 June 1829'). The History of Western Australia page adds that Lockyer formally took possession of the portion west of the 129th meridian on 21 January 1827.
1832: the Swan River Colony is renamed Western Australia. 'on 6 February 1832, the Swan River Colony was renamed the Colony of Western Australia'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: Western Australia as it stood in 1900

ledger.note: 1901: Western Australia federates. 'On 1 January 1901, following a proclamation by Queen Victoria, Western Australia' joined the Commonwealth of Australia. The State of Western Australia is carried by the commonwealth-of-australia dossier.

wars.name: Pinjarra massacre
belligerents: Indigenous Australians of the Pinjarra district
wars.outcome: The Pinjarra massacre 'occurred on 28 October 1834 in Pinjarra, Western Australia' (Pinjarra massacre page, lead and infobox). No border moved; the Indigenous side was stateless.
wars.note: Reviewer fix (review-oc-02-x): the Australian frontier wars page dates Pinjarra to 28 October 1833, the Pinjarra massacre page to 28 October 1834 (infobox and lead); the dedicated page is followed. The larger Australian frontier wars in Western Australia run on for decades (not dated on the page).

certainty.note: The only land border is the 129th meridian east, fixed by the 1825 extension of New South Wales (Territorial evolution of Australia) and unchanged to 1901; it is a legal line, surveyed on the ground only much later. Settlement outside the Swan River and southwest districts was thin throughout.

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. 4 pages used: Swan River Colony, Colony of Western Australia (the page opened under that URL is the History of Western Australia article), Territorial evolution of Australia, Australian frontier wars.
Dates differ: Territorial evolution gives 2 May 1829 for the Swan River Colony's founding; the Swan River Colony page's infobox gives 17 June 1829 and its text gives 2 May as Fremantle's claim. The dossier starts at 17 June (month 6). The Swan River page also lists 'Disestablishment 6 February 1832' (the renaming) in its infobox: the colony continued as the Colony of Western Australia, so a rename event is used and the state is one dossier. Not on the pages opened: convict transportation from 1850 (the History page says 'Western Australia became a penal colony in 1850' and '9,000 convicts' by 1868), responsible government in 1890 ('Western Australia gained the right of self-government in 1890'). Neither changes a border. The Perth founding date (12 August 1829) is not on the pages. The Colony of Western Australia URL redirected to the History of Western Australia article, so the infobox facts (1832 to 1901) are from there.
